design_point.reference_machine: Laptop with an SSD and at least 8 GB of memory

epics.title: Library intake
epics.goal: Turn folders of audio files the user already has into a catalogue the app can reopen.

epics.title: Metadata
epics.goal: Give every track a usable title, artist, and album, including files whose tags are incomplete.

epics.title: Lookup and browsing
epics.goal: Find a track quickly once the collection is past a few thousand songs, which is the pain that started this project.

epics.title: Playback
epics.goal: Play the local file from the library, the queue, or a playlist.

epics.title: Playlists
epics.goal: Let the user organize tracks without depending on a streaming account.

epics.title: Library health
epics.goal: Show broken files, thin tags, and likely duplicates instead of hiding them.

epics.title: Quality attributes and scope
epics.goal: Lock the qualities that make this a local library, and record what this term will leave alone.

requirements.title: Choose library folders
requirements.story: As a collector, I want to choose the folders that hold my music, so that the app uses the files I already have.
acceptance_criteria: The user can add a folder and see it listed as a library root.
The user can add more than one library root, and every root stays in the list.
The user can remove a library root from the list.
requirements.notes: The author's complaint is about music they can already store locally. The library starts from those folders.

requirements.title: Scan folders for audio files
requirements.story: As a collector, I want LocalShelf to walk my library folders and find audio files, so that I do not have to import songs one at a time.
acceptance_criteria: A scan visits files under each library root, including nested folders.
Each supported audio file becomes a track in the catalogue.
Files that are not audio are skipped and do not appear as tracks.

requirements.title: Support common audio formats
requirements.story: As a collector, I want MP3, FLAC, AAC in M4A, Ogg Vorbis, and WAV files to enter the library, so that a normal personal collection can be indexed without converting it first.
acceptance_criteria: A folder containing those five formats produces a track for each file.
A file with an unsupported extension is skipped and counted with the other skipped files.
The track record stores which format the file is.
requirements.notes: These are the formats most likely to show up in a personal archive. The list is an assumption and is called out as an open question.

requirements.title: Persist the catalogue locally
requirements.story: As a collector, I want the catalogue saved on this computer, so that opening the app tomorrow does not mean scanning thousands of files again.
acceptance_criteria: After a completed scan, quitting and reopening the app shows the same tracks without a full scan.
Each track has a stable id that stays the same across restarts while its file remains at the same path.
The catalogue is stored on the local machine.
requirements.notes: Slow lookup in streaming apps is painful partly because the library is not a durable local index. Persistence is what makes later searches fast.

requirements.title: Reconcile the library on rescan
requirements.story: As a collector, I want a rescan to pick up new, changed, and removed files, so that the catalogue follows the folders as I add albums.
acceptance_criteria: A file under a library root that was not in the catalogue becomes a new track.
A file whose size or modification time changed is updated.
A file at a known path with the same size and modification time is not fully re-read.
A file that is no longer at its indexed path is marked missing and kept in the catalogue for REQ-031.
requirements.notes: Matching a moved file to its old track is deliberately unresolved. See open questions. This pass treats identity as the file path.

requirements.title: Show scan progress and allow cancel
requirements.story: As a collector, I want to see how far a scan has gotten and to cancel it, so that a large folder does not feel stuck.
acceptance_criteria: While a scan runs, the interface shows how many files have been visited.
The user can cancel a scan that is still running.
A cancelled scan leaves the previous catalogue usable.

requirements.title: Tolerate unreadable files
requirements.story: As a collector, I want one bad file to be reported and skipped, so that a single unreadable song does not throw away the rest of the scan.
acceptance_criteria: If a file cannot be read, the scan continues with the next file.
The finished scan reports how many files failed and lists their paths.
A failed file does not appear as a playable track.

requirements.title: Read embedded metadata
requirements.story: As an organizer, I want title, artist, album, album artist, track number, disc number, year, genre, and duration read from each file, so that browsing uses the information already stored in the music.
acceptance_criteria: A correctly tagged file shows those fields in the catalogue.
Duration is available for a supported file even when the text tags are empty.
A missing tag is stored as empty and does not cause the scan of that file to fail.

requirements.title: Fall back to file and folder names
requirements.story: As an organizer, I want a sensible title and artist when tags are missing, so that untagged rips still show up as named tracks.
acceptance_criteria: A file with no title tag displays a title taken from the filename.
A file with no artist tag displays an artist taken from a parent folder name when one is available.
Embedded tags win over filename and folder guesses whenever the tag is present.
requirements.notes: Large personal collections almost always include badly tagged files. Search has to see these fallback names, which is why REQ-014 depends on this item.

requirements.title: Group tracks into albums
requirements.story: As a listener, I want tracks that belong together to show up as one album, so that I can play a record instead of a flat list of files.
acceptance_criteria: Tracks that share album artist and album name are presented as one album.
Track number and disc number determine the order inside that album.
Tracks with no album name are still reachable in the library and are grouped apart from named albums.

requirements.title: Display cover art
requirements.story: As a listener, I want album art on the album and on the now-playing view, so that a large library is recognizable at a glance.
acceptance_criteria: If a file contains an embedded picture, that picture is shown for its album.
If there is no embedded picture and the album folder contains a cover image, that image is used.
An album with no picture still appears in the library with a plain placeholder.

requirements.title: Edit metadata without rewriting audio
requirements.story: As an organizer, I want to correct a title or artist inside LocalShelf, so that the library reads correctly while the audio file itself stays untouched.
acceptance_criteria: The user can set title, artist, album, album artist, track number, year, and genre for a track.
After a restart, the edited values are still what search and browse show.
The audio file's bytes are unchanged by the edit.
A later rescan does not wipe the edit while the file is unchanged.
requirements.notes: Rewriting audio files can damage a collection. Corrections live in the catalogue unless the user later chooses REQ-013.

requirements.title: Write metadata back to the file on confirmation
requirements.story: As an organizer, I want an explicit action that writes my corrections into the audio file, so that other players see the same tags.
acceptance_criteria: Tags change on disk only after the user confirms a write for that file.
A failed write leaves the previous file in place and shows an error.
After a successful write, a rescan reads the new tags.
requirements.notes: Kept as Could because a bad writer can ruin files. REQ-012 is the safe version and is enough for a first release.

requirements.title: Search the library while typing
requirements.story: As a collector with thousands of tracks, I want matches to appear as I type a title, artist, album, or genre, so that finding a song stays quick after the library has outgrown a streaming app.
acceptance_criteria: The search matches title, artist, album, and genre, ignoring letter case.
Each change to the query replaces the previous results.
An empty query shows the library without a search filter.
A track with empty tags is still findable by the fallback title and artist from REQ-009.
The speed of this search meets REQ-039.
requirements.notes: This is the center of the project. The author reported that Spotify, Deezer, and Apple Music all become slow to look through once a library passes roughly 3,000 songs.

requirements.title: Browse by artist and album
requirements.story: As a listener, I want to open an artist and then an album, so that I can move through a large collection without searching when I already know whose record I want.
acceptance_criteria: The library can be opened as a list of artists.
Choosing an artist shows that artist's albums.
Choosing an album shows its tracks in album order.

requirements.title: Browse by genre
requirements.story: As a listener, I want a genre list, so that I can start from a mood when I do not have an artist in mind.
acceptance_criteria: Genres present in the catalogue are listed.
Choosing a genre shows the tracks tagged with it.
Tracks with no genre appear under an unlabeled group.

requirements.title: Sort track lists
requirements.story: As a listener, I want to sort a list of tracks by title, artist, album, year, duration, or date added, so that a long result list has a predictable order.
acceptance_criteria: Each of those six sort keys can be applied to a track list.
The same key can switch between ascending and descending order.
The chosen sort remains in effect while the user pages through that list.

requirements.title: Filter track lists
requirements.story: As an organizer, I want to narrow a list by genre, year range, and file format, so that I can work on one slice of a large collection.
acceptance_criteria: A genre filter hides tracks outside that genre.
A year range hides tracks outside the range, and tracks with no year are excluded from a year-bounded list.
A format filter hides other formats.
Clearing filters restores the list that the current sort would show.

requirements.title: Show recently added and recently played
requirements.story: As a listener, I want to see what arrived recently and what I played recently, so that a large library still has an easy way back in.
acceptance_criteria: Recently added lists tracks by the time they first entered the catalogue, newest first.
Recently played lists tracks by the last time playback started, newest first.
Both lists survive a restart.

requirements.title: Search and browse during a scan
requirements.story: As a collector, I want to search what is already indexed while a rescan is still running, so that a big import does not lock me out of the library.
acceptance_criteria: Search and artist browsing stay available during a rescan.
Results reflect tracks indexed so far, plus the previous catalogue.
A track that the running scan has not visited yet can still be found if it was already in the catalogue.

requirements.title: Play audio with transport controls
requirements.story: As a listener, I want to play, pause, seek, and skip the local file, so that the library is something I can listen to and not only search.
acceptance_criteria: Choosing a track starts playback of that file.
Pause and resume return to the same position in the file.
The user can seek within the current track.
Next and previous move within the current context: an album, a playlist, a queue, or the current result list.
A missing or unreadable file does not start playback and is reported on screen.
requirements.notes: A fast index alone would not answer the request for a better experience than the streaming apps. Playback of the local file is part of the first release.

requirements.title: Keep an ordered play queue
requirements.story: As a listener, I want a queue I can add to, reorder, and trim, so that I can line up songs from different albums.
acceptance_criteria: The user can add a track to the end of the queue or insert it so that it plays next.
The user can remove a queued track and drag or otherwise reorder the queue.
When the current track ends, playback continues with the next queued track.

requirements.title: Control volume
requirements.story: As a listener, I want volume and mute inside the app, so that I can adjust playback without leaving the library.
acceptance_criteria: A volume control changes the loudness of playback.
Mute silences playback and a second activation restores the previous level.
The volume setting is still in effect for the next track.

requirements.title: Show now playing
requirements.story: As a listener, I want the current track's title, artist, album, and position visible while it plays, so that I can tell what I am hearing in a large library.
acceptance_criteria: While a track plays, title, artist, and album are visible.
Elapsed time and duration update during playback.
When cover art is available from REQ-011, it is shown here. When it is not, the metadata still shows.

requirements.title: Resume long tracks
requirements.story: As a listener, I want a long track to remember where I stopped, so that a mix or a live recording can be continued later.
acceptance_criteria: Stopping playback of a track longer than 15 minutes stores the position.
Playing that track again offers the stored position.
The user can discard the stored position and start from the beginning.

requirements.title: Create and delete playlists
requirements.story: As a collector, I want to create, rename, and delete playlists stored on this computer, so that my organization is not tied to a streaming account.
acceptance_criteria: The user can create a named playlist and see it in the playlist list.
The user can rename a playlist.
Deleting a playlist removes it from the list and asks for confirmation.
Playlists are still present after a restart.

requirements.title: Edit playlist contents
requirements.story: As a collector, I want to add, remove, and reorder tracks in a playlist, so that the playlist matches the sequence I want to hear.
acceptance_criteria: A track from the catalogue can be added to a playlist.
A track can be removed from a playlist without deleting the file or the catalogue entry.
Tracks in a playlist can be reordered, and the new order is what playback uses.
The same track can appear twice in one playlist.

requirements.title: Play a playlist in order
requirements.story: As a listener, I want to start a playlist and have it play in the saved order, so that a playlist is a listening sequence and not only a list of names.
acceptance_criteria: Starting a playlist plays its first available track.
When a track ends, the next playlist track starts.
A missing file in the middle of a playlist is skipped and reported, and playback continues with the next available track.

requirements.title: Export a playlist as M3U
requirements.story: As a collector, I want to export a playlist as M3U, so that another desktop player can open the same sequence of files.
acceptance_criteria: Export writes an M3U file the user chooses a location for.
The file lists the playlist's tracks in playlist order, using their paths.
A missing track is either omitted or marked in a way the export summary explains.

requirements.title: Build a smart playlist from filters
requirements.story: As an organizer, I want a playlist that stays filled by saved filter rules, so that a slice of the library updates itself as files are added.
acceptance_criteria: The user can save genre, year, and format rules as a smart playlist.
Opening the smart playlist shows the tracks that currently match.
After a rescan adds a matching track, the smart playlist includes it without a manual edit.

requirements.title: Track missing files
requirements.story: As a collector, I want missing files called out in one place, so that a moved folder or a disconnected drive does not look like a randomly broken library.
acceptance_criteria: Tracks whose files were not found on the last rescan appear in a missing-files view.
A missing track cannot be played, and the interface says the file is missing.
When a later rescan finds the file at the same path, the track leaves the missing-files view and becomes playable again.

requirements.title: Keep user data when a file disappears
requirements.story: As a collector, I want a playlist to remember a track while its file is missing, so that reconnecting a drive does not force me to rebuild the playlist.
acceptance_criteria: A playlist entry for a missing track remains in the playlist and is labeled unavailable.
The entry is not deleted just because a rescan failed to find the file.
When the file is found again at the same path, that playlist entry plays without the user adding it again.
requirements.notes: Metadata overrides from REQ-012, once that item exists, should follow the same rule and survive a temporary disappearance.

requirements.title: Flag incomplete metadata
requirements.story: As an organizer, I want a list of tracks that still have no real title or artist after tag reading and filename fallback, so that I know which files need attention.
acceptance_criteria: The view includes tracks whose title is empty even after REQ-009.
The view includes tracks whose artist is empty even after REQ-009.
Opening a row shows the file path.

requirements.title: Suggest duplicate recordings
requirements.story: As an organizer, I want groups of tracks that look like the same recording, so that I can clean copies that piled up across folders.
acceptance_criteria: Tracks with the same normalized artist and title, and durations within two seconds, are offered as a duplicate group.
The user can open each file's path from the group.
The app does not delete any file as part of showing the group.
requirements.notes: Suggestion only. Deleting audio files is not part of this requirement.

requirements.title: Confirm duplicates by content hash
requirements.story: As an organizer, I want a content hash on a suspected duplicate group, so that I can tell identical files from two different recordings that share a name.
acceptance_criteria: From a duplicate group, the user can ask for a hash of each file's audio contents.
Files with the same hash are marked as identical content.
Files with different hashes stay in the group as name matches only.

requirements.title: Work fully offline
requirements.statement: Search, browsing, playlists, and playback of indexed files work with the network disconnected.
acceptance_criteria: With the network disabled, an existing library still opens.
Search, artist browsing, playlist playback, and file playback still work on that library.
No Must-priority action waits on a network response before it succeeds or fails.
requirements.notes: The author's point was that a local copy behaves better than the offline mode in Spotify, Deezer, and Apple Music. Offline behavior is a product requirement, not an extra.

requirements.title: Keep the library on the device
requirements.statement: LocalShelf has no account and does not send library contents or listening history off the machine.
acceptance_criteria: A person can scan, search, and play with no sign-in step.
File paths, tags, and play history are not transmitted to a server by any Must-priority feature.
The catalogue from REQ-004 remains readable on the machine with the network disabled.

requirements.title: Leave streaming catalogues and DRM out of scope
requirements.statement: This term's product plays audio files the user already has. It does not connect to Spotify, Deezer, Apple Music, or any other streaming catalogue, and it does not remove DRM.
acceptance_criteria: The backlog for the term contains no story whose acceptance depends on a streaming service login or API.
The app has no feature whose purpose is to download a streamed catalogue or to strip protection from a file.
requirements.notes: The original problem names three streaming services. Rebuilding or plugging into those catalogues is a different product, and it is the wrong size for one semester. The part that is in scope is the local library those apps handle poorly.

requirements.title: Meet the search latency target
requirements.statement: On the design-point library, the first search results are visible within 100 milliseconds of each query change once the catalogue is already loaded.
acceptance_criteria: The design-point library contains 10,000 tracks in a mix of the supported formats, with tags on most files.
The measurement starts when the query text changes and stops when the first results are painted. The catalogue is already loaded, and no rescan is running.
Across a set of 20 queries that includes one-character, three-character, and full-title queries, the median time is under 100 milliseconds on the reference laptop.
A design that re-reads every audio file on each keystroke does not satisfy this requirement.
requirements.notes: The need comes from the problem statement. The number 100 milliseconds, and the library size of 10,000, are proposed targets for the later test plan. They sit above the roughly 3,000 tracks where streaming apps already felt slow, and they can be revised after the first measurement.

requirements.title: Open a large library quickly
requirements.statement: Opening an existing design-point library reaches an interactive track or artist view within 3 seconds, without waiting for a full rescan.
acceptance_criteria: The library has already been indexed and contains 10,000 tracks.
The clock starts at process launch and stops when the user can type a search or open an artist.
On the reference laptop this takes 3 seconds or less.
Launch does not start a blocking rescan before the view becomes interactive.

requirements.title: Stay responsive while indexing
requirements.statement: A rescan does not freeze playback or the library view that is already on screen.
acceptance_criteria: Starting a rescan while a track is playing does not stop that track.
While the rescan runs, the current view still scrolls and accepts a click on a track that is already indexed.
The interface shows that a scan is in progress so the user can tell new files may still be arriving.

requirements.title: Keep the previous index if a scan fails
requirements.statement: A failed rescan leaves the last successful catalogue in place.
acceptance_criteria: If the process is stopped in the middle of a rescan, the next launch opens the last successful catalogue.
Tracks that the failed scan had not finished reconciling keep their previous metadata and playlist membership.
The app tells the user that the last scan did not finish.

requirements.title: Leave multi-device sync out of scope
requirements.statement: Syncing the catalogue or the audio files across phones, laptops, or a cloud drive is out of scope this term.
acceptance_criteria: No Must or Should requirement depends on a second device or a cloud account.

requirements.title: Leave social features out of scope
requirements.statement: Sharing, followers, and collaborative playlists are out of scope this term.
acceptance_criteria: The first release has no account-to-account sharing feature.

requirements.title: Leave a mobile client out of scope
requirements.statement: The term project is a desktop application. A phone or tablet client is out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Requirements in this backlog are written for a desktop window, keyboard, and local filesystem.
requirements.notes: Which desktop operating systems are in the first test pass is an open question. The author's machine is Windows.

requirements.title: Leave podcasts and video out of scope
requirements.statement: Podcasts and video files are out of scope. The library is music files in the formats from REQ-003.
acceptance_criteria: Video files and podcast feeds are not indexed as tracks by any Must requirement.
